summary: The Central African Republic's embassy in Washington says all travelers must apply for a visa for entry; citizens of fellow CEMAC states (Cameroon, Chad, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea) enter visa-free under the Community's free-movement arrangements. The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against travel to the country.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for the Central African Republic; the embassy's visa document list does not include it. The Government of Canada says health care is very limited and only available in Bangui, that medical expenses must generally be paid before treatment, and advises insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

notes: The UK FCDO says it is only legal to buy diamonds or precious stones through government-authorised agents.

The UK FCDO says you often need permission to take photos in public places, and that photographing government property, uniformed officers or military installations and personnel can get you detained, fined and your camera confiscated.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says the economy is cash-based: only Bangui's major hotels accept credit cards, ATMs are found only in a few banks and hotels in Bangui, and currency can be exchanged only in Bangui and Berbérati. Australia's Smartraveller says very few ATMs are available in Bangui and that most hotels, supermarkets and restaurants catering to foreigners accept only cash.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel outside Bangui and all but essential travel to Bangui; Canada and Australia advise against all travel. The FCDO says armed groups continue to occupy areas in the north and south-east, and that homicides, kidnapping and carjacking are frequent outside Bangui; it advises taking professional security advice.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the Central African Republic except Bangui, and against all but essential travel to Bangui; Australia advises against all travel. The FCDO warns that travel insurance could be invalidated if you travel against its advice.

The visa must be obtained in advance from a Central African embassy. The embassy in Washington gives standard processing as 5–10 business days on its application page; its visa notice page says requests take 72 hours, with express processing in 24–48 hours for USD 50 more.

Australia's Smartraveller says very few ATMs are available in Bangui and that most hotels, supermarkets and restaurants catering to foreigners accept only cash; Canada says currency can be exchanged only in Bangui and Berbérati.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Central African Republic?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold a passport from a CEMAC state (Cameroon, Chad, Congo, Gabon or Equatorial Guinea). Everyone else must obtain a visa in advance from a Central African embassy.

faq.question: How do I get a Central African Republic visa?
faq.answer: Apply at a Central African embassy. The embassy in Washington accepts applications in person or by mail and asks for a flight itinerary, a copy of the yellow fever vaccination card and an invitation letter or hotel reservation; its application page gives 5–10 business days for processing, and its visa notice page 72 hours.

faq.question: Is the Central African Republic safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. The UK FCDO advises against all travel outside Bangui and all but essential travel to Bangui, and Australia advises against all travel. Australia says outbreaks of intercommunal violence and armed conflict can happen without warning throughout the country, including in Bangui.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for the Central African Republic?
faq.answer: Yes. The embassy in Washington says yellow fever immunization is required, and the UK FCDO says you must have a yellow fever certificate to pass border control. WHO lists the requirement for travellers aged 9 months and over.

faq.question: Which nationalities can enter the Central African Republic without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of the CEMAC bloc — Cameroon, Chad, the Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea — enter visa-free under the Community's free-movement arrangements. All other nationalities need an embassy visa.
